inputs.acceptance_evidence: Full-text-searched all 3 pinned acquired OpenRaster spec sources for 'metadata' (0 hits in all 3) and 'reference' (4 hits, all describing the src attribute as an archive-member file path, zero describing a cross-element reference concept). execution_steps: 1. Read SAL-ORA-OBL-EC8D65524EB96820's own rule_text directly from the obligation register (not just the evidence file's paraphrase): 'Provide transactional add, replace, move, rename, and remove operations for groups, layers, assets, and metadata; maintain references and invalidate stale derived views.' -- confirmed 'metadata' and 'references' are named at the MUST/STABLE_REQUIRED level, not merely implied by a looser missing_behavior summary.

2. Full-text-searched all 3 pinned acquired OpenRaster spec sources (.local/format-contracts/acquired/ora/src-ora-00{1,2,3}.bin) for the literal string 'metadata' (case-insensitive): 0 occurrences in any of the 3 files. Confirmed OpenRaster is a ZIP of mimetype + stack.xml + raster assets with no dedicated metadata element or schema, unlike ODF's own meta.xml.

3. Searched the same 3 sources for 'reference': 4 occurrences, all in src-ora-002.bin. Read each hit's own surrounding line directly: all 4 describe the src attribute as an archive-member FILE PATH ('image data files referenced by stack.xml, typically layer*.png', 'Files must be referenced in stack.xml by their full path relative to the [archive root]', 'All files inside this directory should be referenced from somewhere', 'The thumbnail file must not be referenced in any .xml file') -- zero hits describing any cross-ELEMENT reference concept (e.g. one layer pointing at another by id) within the model tree itself.

4. Cross-checked against model/stack.py's own validate_src and the OraLayer/OraText src field: confirmed src is a static, archive-root-relative path string, computed once at parse time, with no dependency on the element's own position in the tree -- renaming, moving, or removing a layer via apply_transaction does not change what that layer's own src value means, so there is nothing for 'reference maintenance' to actually repair even if a cross-element reference concept existed.

5. Concluded both 'metadata' and 'maintain references' are ungrounded authoring artifacts -- the same disposition already independently established for this obligation's own sibling, ORA-MASK-001 (same authority_fact_ids cluster including SAL-ORA-00008), whose own missing_behavior explicitly documents 'the word mask appears zero times across all three pinned OpenRaster spec sources.'

6. Explicitly verified the 3rd remaining clause, stale-derived-view invalidation, is NOT part of this finding -- re-confirmed no pixel-compositing/rendering infrastructure exists anywhere in the ora package (matching ORA-UTF8-BASELINE-CITATION-AUDIT-PROOF's own earlier finding this session that the only render() in the codebase generates XML text, not pixels), a genuine dependency block on ORA-RENDER-001/ORA-COMPOSITE-001, not an authoring artifact.

7. Updated the obligation's own implemented_behavior (adding the finding, dated FF6-EVENT-000318) and missing_behavior (precisely distinguishing the 2 now-confirmed-ungrounded clauses from the 1 genuinely-blocked clause) in shared/format-contracts/implementation-evidence/ora.yaml. Left status as partial, matching the ORA-MASK-001 precedent of not force-closing an obligation whose own rule_text still names an ungrounded clause.
8. Registered a new execution_evidence entry (ORA-EDIT-METADATA-REFERENCE-GROUNDING-AUDIT-PROOF) documenting the full finding, referenced by the obligation's own execution_evidence_ids.
9. Ran the full ora suite to confirm zero regression (349 passed, unchanged -- no source or test files were touched, this is a pure evidence-grounding correction).
